- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Siege of Orléans was a turning point in the Hundred Years' War between England and France, taking place between October 1428 and May 1429.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Orléans was strategically important as it was the gateway to the rest of France.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The English were led by the Duke of Bedford and had captured many French cities including Rouen, Paris, and Chartres.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Joan of Arc, a young peasant girl from Domrémy in Lorraine, claimed to have visions of saints and angels instructing her to aid the French king and lead the army.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Joan of Arc arrived in Orléans on April 29, 1429, and inspired the French troops to fight.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The English withdrew from Orléans on May 8, 1429, marking a turning point in the war.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Joan of Arc was ultimately captured by the English and burned at the stake for heresy in 1431.
- [USER] User was surprised to learn about Joan of Arc's significant role in the Hundred Years' War.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Joan of Arc became a symbol of French nationalism and resistance against the English, and her legacy has been revered in French history.
